prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: A 2019 audit found that, during the previous year, the library had ______ the program.

worlds.passage: For twenty years, a county library tracked every book and borrower with catalog software that its own technicians had written. In 2018 patrons began searching a vendor's catalog on new screens, and the old program's icon vanished from every desk. The auditors nonetheless found the old code intact on a basement server, beside a copy of that year's records and a note from the technicians explaining how to switch it back on within an hour. A 2019 audit found that, during the previous year, the library had ______ the program.
worlds.explanation: The old program was taken out of use yet kept intact and ready to restart, so the library had "mothballed" it. "Patched" fails because the code was found intact, not repaired. "Outsourced" fails because nobody was running it at all once its icon vanished, and "repackaged" fails because it sat on a basement server rather than being presented to anyone in a new form.

patched.why: code left intact had not been repaired

outsourced.why: a program no one uses is not being run by an outside firm

repackaged.why: it was stored, not offered to anyone in a new form

worlds.passage: For twenty years, a county library tracked every book and borrower with catalog software that its own technicians had written. Patrons in 2018 still searched the same gray screens they had used since 1999, and the search still froze now and then. The auditors counted forty-one small changes to the code that year, each dated within a day of a borrower's complaint about a frozen search and each signed by one of the library's technicians. A 2019 audit found that, during the previous year, the library had ______ the program.
worlds.explanation: Small code changes made right after each complaint about freezing show that the technicians had "patched" the program. "Mothballed" fails because patrons still used it. "Outsourced" fails because the library's own technicians made the changes, and "repackaged" fails because patrons saw the same screens they had used since 1999.
